chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdul Aziz al-Muhtadi, who raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), saying:
There is no one except that there is a vein of leprosy in him, so melt it with the turnip.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical significance of the turnip in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of a 'vein of leprosy' to signify the inherent impurities or minor ailments present in every human constitution, prescribing the turnip (salsaj) as a potent natural remedy to purify the body. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia emphasis on the medicinal wisdom of common foods as part of the Prophetic tradition (Sunnah) for maintaining physical and spiritual cleanliness.
